سَخِينٌ : see سُخْنٌ, in three places. [See also a saying of ' Amr Ibn-Kulthoom cited in the first paragraph of art. سخو and سخى.] ―
-b2- Also, (K,) or سَخِينُ العَيْنِ, (S, MA, L,) A man whose eye is [hot, or heated, or inflamed, by weeping, or by grief or sorrow; or] hot in its tears. (S, * MA, L, * K. *) ―
-b3- And ضَرْبٌ سَخِينٌ, (K,) or ↓ سِخِّينٌ , (L,) (assumed tropical:) A hot, [i. e.] painful, smiting. (L, K. [Both are probably correct: that the latter is so is shown by what here follows.]) Ibn-Mukbil says, “↓ ضَرْبًا تَرَامَتْ بِهِ الأَبْطَالُ سِخِّينَا
” [A smiting which the brave men cast, one at another, burning, or painful: the measure (بَسِيط) requires us to read the last word thus, with tesh-deed to the خ]. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
